segments.title: A clearer way to review returns
segments.spoken: Return requests aren't always clear. Clocked Return Lab helps a support agent find the important details and see what to check next. This demo uses made-up customer messages. Nothing gets refunded or sent.

segments.title: A straightforward return
segments.spoken: In our first example, a customer says an unopened lamp arrived twelve days ago. Under the sample thirty-day policy, the app suggests approval. The agent would still need to check the real order.

segments.title: See where each detail came from
segments.spoken: You can open the details to see what the app found. The date, item and refund request are highlighted in the original message. That shows where the information came from. It doesn't prove the customer is right.

segments.title: Some cases need a person
segments.spoken: Next is a request about broken headphones. The delivery date is missing and the item may be defective. Rather than guessing, the app sends the case to a support agent for review.

segments.title: Outside the example window
segments.spoken: Here, a customer says an unused item arrived fifty-eight days ago. That's outside the sample return window, so the app suggests declining. A person still needs to check the store policy and the customer's legal rights.

segments.title: Where Clocked fits
segments.spoken: Now let's look at live mode, which I won't run in this video. The integration uses Protect to mask personal details, Guard to screen suspicious input, Extract to find information in the message, and Decide to assess specific questions. Our own checks then determine which recommendation to show.

segments.title: The agent makes the final call
segments.spoken: That's the idea behind Clocked Return Lab. It gives support staff a suggested next step and lets them check the reasons. This demo doesn't call Clocked or change a customer order. The actual integration and tests are available on GitHub.
